label: def:adelic-substrate
title: Adelic substrate $\mathbb{A}$
html:
Definition. Adelic substrate \mathbb{A}

Definition. The adelic substrate of the QOU framework is the ring of adeles of \mathbb{Q},

  \mathbb{A}
  \;=\;
  \mathbb{R} \;\times\; \prod_{p}{}^{\!\!\prime}\;\mathbb{Q}_p,

the restricted product of the archimedean completion \mathbb{R} with all p-adic completions \mathbb{Q}_p (restriction: almost all components lie in the maximal compact subring \mathbb{Z}_p).

Each non-archimedean place p corresponds to a localized quantum geometric state of the substrate: a specific q-deformation evaluated at a primitive root of unity, equivalently a Kummer level in the Habiro / cyclotomic completion (algebraic quantum volume). The archimedean place \infty — the \mathbb{R} component — is the laboratory continuum, accessible only through the classical limit functor and the archimedean realization functor.

The motivation for replacing \mathbb{R} by \mathbb{A}, and the Tate-integral form of the global substrate observables, are developed in the follow-on remark.
